critical_path.basis: No bound duration/cost estimates. Use causal DAG and ready frontiers, not fabricated schedule.

local_slice_semantics: K01–K12 are implementation/fixture preparation slices, not new business milestones or proof of canonical DONE. They can proceed under bound code authorization before late runtime/binding gates close. Canonical action dependencies govern closure. G00 refreshes snapshot; it does not reopen historical A00 acquisition.

P1: Actual source-bound required CI or governance-approved equivalent
Runtime owner/readiness faults on built artifacts in intended topology; static flags are insufficient
P2: All15acceptance+20zero-tolerance clauses with nonempty valid cohorts
Actual consumer delivery and PG recovery; schema alone insufficient
P3: MetaEditor/EA include+binary binding and disposable combined migrations/race proofs
P4: D0 rejection may close outcome but cannot claim fill
P5: Natural valid occurrences, not manufactured manual signals
P6: Known unremediated mandatory safety defects invalidate applicable prior gates; complete review cannot launder them

ready_frontier_rule: After G00, import valid session authority and existing scoped evidence. Select nonblocked local K slices whose hard parents pass; never treat BLOCKED canonical node as executable.

predicate_binding_rules.scope_rule: A satisfied predicate is scoped by subject/release ID, source/config/schema/policy/target and relevant time validity. It is never a reusable global PASS for changed artifacts.
predicate_binding_rules.release_readiness: C05 closure and current release.candidate_gates_bound are required before target migration/deployment. Each subsequent child/natural release is rebound.
predicate_binding_rules.conditional_mutation: No-op verification does not require admin mutation authority. Needed changes reuse valid scoped authority or await one concrete decision.
predicate_binding_rules.runtime_constraints: Host availability/bootstrap may precede program acceptance; source policy-contract mapping may precede actual consumer runtime and active account-risk binding. These downstream requirements retain explicit owners.
